key_insight: Cross-entropy imitation can be misaligned in verifiable tasks, while entropy-regularized cross-entropy helps concentrate probability on supported outputs and better matches verifier accuracy.
engineering_relevance: For theorem proving and code generation systems, this suggests a simple training objective change can improve end-to-end correctness when many valid solutions exist.
method: Prove a learning-theoretic counterexample where standard CE selects a policy with worse verifier risk.
Motivate support control as the right target, then approximate it with token-level Shannon entropy.
Train with entropy-regularized cross-entropy (ER-CE) instead of plain CE.
evidence_signal: Across mathematical reasoning and code-generation benchmarks, the abstract reports that entropy-regularized training consistently improves verifier accuracy over standard cross-entropy.
watch_item: Token-level entropy is only a proxy for support size, so gains may depend on how well the regularizer matches the verifier’s notion of valid outputs.
paper_title: Entropy Regularization: A Free Correction to Cross-Entropy for Verified Demonstrations
